rules.quote: powershell -File $CONFIG/scripts/hook-startup.ps1

rules.quote: Append ONE line to `memory/lessons_learned.md`

rules.quote: Format: `YYYY-MM-DD | {topic} | {what was wrong} → {what fixed it}`

rules.quote: powershell -File $CONFIG/scripts/update-session-yaml.ps1 -Decision "<text>"

rules.quote: Writes to KG: Decision node + relation to project

rules.quote: Update `memory/project_active.md`

rules.quote: Write KG node (type: state_change, name: {change})

rules.quote: Notify relevant agents via mail if applicable

rules.quote: Log error to session_log + KG:

rules.quote: Link to relevant Decision/Task nodes

rules.quote: All scripts are fire-and-forget (non-blocking)

rules.quote: KG writes use retry up to 3 times on failure

rules.quote: `session.yaml` is the single source of truth for session state

rules.rule: Enable Actions in the repository settings.

rules.quote: Let CI catch errors before deploy
rules.rule: Let CI catch errors before deploying.

rules.rule: When tests fail, have GitHub post a PR comment saying "❌ Tests failed, no deploy".

rules.rule: To skip e2e tests, add `--ignore=tests/e2e` to the pytest command.

rules.rule: If any required file is missing during project initialization, exit with an error listing the missing files.

rules.rule: You may adopt the references/ split pattern, scripts/ black-box helpers, evaluation QA pairs, and contribution guidelines from the awesome-agent-skills ecosystem.

rules.quote: Reference architecture only.

rules.quote: Redirect output to NUL (Windows black hole) to detach the process.
rules.rule: Redirect a background server's output to NUL to detach the process from the shell.

rules.quote: NEVER: `Start-Process php artisan serve` without redirect — blocks forever.
rules.rule: Never start `php artisan serve` with `Start-Process` without redirecting its output.

rules.quote: NEVER: `php artisan serve > /dev/null 2>&1 &` — bash background, not PowerShell.
rules.rule: Never use the bash background form `php artisan serve > /dev/null 2>&1 &` in PowerShell.

rules.quote:
ALWAYS for PHP/Laravel servers:
    Start-Process -NoNewWindow -WindowStyle Hidden php -ArgumentList "artisan","serve","--port=XXXX" -RedirectStandardOutput NUL -RedirectStandardError NUL
rules.rule: When starting PHP/Laravel servers, always use Start-Process with -NoNewWindow, -WindowStyle Hidden, and stdout/stderr redirected to NUL.

rules.quote:
For Node/Express servers:
    Start-Process -NoNewWindow -WindowStyle Hidden node -ArgumentList "server.js","--port=XXXX" -RedirectStandardOutput NUL -RedirectStandardError NUL
rules.rule: When starting Node/Express servers, use Start-Process with -NoNewWindow, -WindowStyle Hidden, and stdout/stderr redirected to NUL.

rules.quote: Alternative: Use `Start-Process -PassThru` to get the PID immediately, which also works.
rules.rule: As an alternative when starting a background server, you may use `Start-Process -PassThru` to obtain the PID immediately.

rules.quote: Always redirect stdout and stderr to NUL when starting background servers:
rules.rule: Always redirect both stdout and stderr to NUL when starting background servers.

rules.quote: **Before starting any background server**, always add `-RedirectStandardOutput NUL -RedirectStandardError NUL`
rules.rule: Before starting any background server, always add `-RedirectStandardOutput NUL` and `-RedirectStandardError NUL` to the start command.

rules.quote: **For the OpenCode coordinator and all agents**, this pattern should be automatic when starting servers
rules.rule: For the OpenCode coordinator and all agents, automatically use this background-server pattern when starting servers.

rules.quote: After starting, wait 3 seconds
rules.rule: After starting a background server, wait 3 seconds before proceeding.

rules.quote: then `Invoke-WebRequest http://127.0.0.1:PORT -UseBasicParsing` to confirm it's up
rules.rule: After starting a background server, run `Invoke-WebRequest http://127.0.0.1:PORT -UseBasicParsing` to confirm it is up.

rules.quote: This pattern should be in the coordinator's permanent workflow.
rules.rule: Include this background-server pattern in the coordinator's permanent workflow.

rules.quote: When any agent needs to start a server, the coordinator should enforce:
rules.rule: When any agent needs to start a server, the coordinator should enforce use of the correct Start-Process command with output redirected to NUL.

rules.quote:
# Kill on specific port (preferred)
Stop-Process -Id (Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8080).OwningProcess -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
rules.rule: When stopping a background server, prefer killing the process on the specific port with `Stop-Process -Id (Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8080).OwningProcess -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`.

rules.quote: Always use this exact shape:
rules.rule: Always format commit messages as `type(scope): subject in imperative mood`, optionally followed by a body.

rules.quote: optional body explaining WHY (not WHAT — the diff shows what)
rules.rule: When a commit body is included, explain WHY the change was made rather than WHAT changed.

rules.quote: ## Types (pick one)
rules.rule: Prefix every commit with exactly one type from the defined list of types.

rules.quote: | `feat` | New user-facing feature |
rules.rule: Use the `feat` type for a commit that adds a new user-facing feature.

rules.quote: | `fix` | Bug fix |
rules.rule: Use the `fix` type for a commit that fixes a bug.

rules.quote: | `refactor` | Code change that doesn't add/fix a feature |
rules.rule: Use the `refactor` type for a code change that neither adds nor fixes a feature.

rules.quote: | `test` | Adding or fixing tests only |
rules.rule: Use the `test` type for commits that only add or fix tests.

rules.quote: | `docs` | README, inline docs, comments |
rules.rule: Use the `docs` type for changes to README, inline docs, or comments.

rules.quote: | `ops` | Railway/Docker/infra/env config |
rules.rule: Use the `ops` type for Railway, Docker, infrastructure, or environment config changes.

rules.quote: | `ci` | GitHub Actions / pipeline only |
rules.rule: Use the `ci` type for changes limited to GitHub Actions or pipeline configuration.

rules.quote: | `chore` | Deps bump, lockfile, formatting — nothing else |
rules.rule: Use the `chore` type only for dependency bumps, lockfile changes, or formatting, and nothing else.

rules.quote: - PRIA: `auth`, `ui`, `api`, `db`, `e2e`, `seed`, `deploy`
rules.rule: When adding a scope to a PRIA commit, use one of: auth, ui, api, db, e2e, seed, deploy.

rules.quote: Omit if change is cross-cutting
rules.rule: Omit the scope when the change is cross-cutting.

rules.quote: When creating ANY commit, the coordinator (or the specialist doing the commit) must follow this format.
rules.rule: The coordinator or the specialist making the commit must follow the commit format for any commit they create.

rules.quote: If the commit doesn't fit one of the types above, the change probably does more than one thing — split it first.
rules.rule: If a change does not fit one of the listed commit types, split the change before committing.

rules.quote: When an HTTP endpoint returns an unexpected status (404, 502, etc.), inspect the response **body** and **headers** before proposing a cause.
rules.rule: When an HTTP endpoint returns an unexpected status (such as 404 or 502), inspect the response body and headers before proposing a cause.

rules.quote: **Before forming a hypothesis, run:**
rules.rule: Before forming a hypothesis about an unexpected HTTP status, run curl commands to capture the status code, body shape, and headers of the response.

rules.quote: **If the response came from your app, the bug is in your code.**
rules.rule: If the response came from your own application, treat the bug as being in your code.

rules.quote: Don't go looking for infrastructure causes.
rules.rule: If the response came from your own application, do not look for infrastructure causes.

rules.quote: Reorder middleware, fix routes, check handler registration — whatever the specific symptom says.
rules.rule: If the response came from your own application, fix the code according to the specific symptom (e.g., reorder middleware, fix routes, or check handler registration).

rules.quote: **If the response came from the proxy/CDN,** then start looking at routing rules, Caddyfile, Nginx config, Cloudflare rules, Railway domain settings, etc.
rules.rule: If the response came from the proxy or CDN, start investigating routing rules, Caddyfile, Nginx config, Cloudflare rules, and Railway domain settings.

rules.quote: If a future session's guidance starts with "the proxy is routing to...", demand the curl evidence before acting on it.
rules.rule: If guidance in a future session claims the proxy is routing requests somewhere, demand the curl evidence before acting on it.

rules.quote: Writing a memory that says "X is a proxy-layer issue" without having verified the body/headers.
rules.rule: Do not write a memory stating something is a proxy-layer issue without having verified the response body and headers.

rules.quote: When writing or editing Playwright tests targeting Railway deploys (PRIA's `tests/test_e2e.py`), don't rely on `page.wait_for_timeout(2_000)` / `3_000` for initial page render.
rules.rule: When writing or editing Playwright tests that target Railway deploys, do not rely on fixed page.wait_for_timeout timers (e.g., 2,000 or 3,000 ms) for initial page render.

rules.quote: For initial page load on Streamlit: use `page.goto(..., wait_until="networkidle", timeout=30_000)`
rules.rule: For initial page load on Streamlit, use page.goto with wait_until="networkidle" and timeout=30_000.

rules.quote: then `page.wait_for_selector("[data-testid='stTextInput'] input", timeout=30_000)`
rules.rule: For initial page load on Streamlit, after page.goto call page.wait_for_selector for the selector "[data-testid='stTextInput'] input" with timeout=30_000.

rules.quote: Timers are fine for *post-action* waits (after a click, while Streamlit rerenders)
rules.rule: Fixed timers are allowed for post-action waits, such as after a click while Streamlit rerenders.

rules.quote: Any time a new e2e test starts by opening the app, add an explicit selector wait, not a timer.
rules.rule: Whenever a new e2e test starts by opening the app, add an explicit selector wait.

rules.quote: Any time a new e2e test starts by opening the app, add an explicit selector wait, not a timer.
rules.rule: Whenever a new e2e test starts by opening the app, do not use a timer as the wait.

rules.quote: Generalizes to any Streamlit-on-Railway project, not just PRIA.
rules.rule: Apply these e2e waiting rules to any Streamlit-on-Railway project, not just PRIA.

rules.quote: If `git push` is rejected with "remote contains work you don't have", do NOT immediately run `git pull`
rules.rule: If `git push` is rejected with "remote contains work you don't have", do not immediately run `git pull`.

rules.quote: do NOT immediately run `git pull` or `git rebase origin/BRANCH`
rules.rule: If `git push` is rejected with "remote contains work you don't have", do not immediately run `git rebase origin/BRANCH`.

rules.quote: Fetch first
rules.rule: When `git push` is rejected because the remote diverged, fetch first before inspecting or acting.

rules.quote: then inspect the divergence
rules.rule: After fetching a divergent remote, inspect the divergence before deciding how to act.

rules.quote: **Fetch, don't pull:**
rules.rule: When handling a divergent remote, fetch instead of pulling.

rules.quote: **Inspect the divergence:**
rules.rule: After fetching a divergent remote, inspect the divergence.

rules.quote: **Look for warning signs:**
rules.rule: When inspecting a divergent remote, look for warning signs of a force-push or squash.

rules.quote: **Compare actual file contents, not just git state:**
rules.rule: When evaluating divergence between local and remote, compare actual file contents, not only git state.

rules.quote: Normalize line endings on Windows (CRLF vs LF trap):
rules.rule: When comparing file contents on Windows, normalize line endings to avoid CRLF vs LF differences.

rules.quote: **Decide intentionally, and announce before acting:**
rules.rule: Decide intentionally how to handle the divergent remote.

rules.quote: **Decide intentionally, and announce before acting:**
rules.rule: Announce your decision before acting on the divergent remote.

rules.quote: **Align local to remote** (you accept the squash): `git reset --hard origin/BRANCH` + manually re-apply your changes + commit + push.
rules.rule: If you accept the remote squash, you may align local to remote by resetting hard to `origin/BRANCH`, manually re-applying your changes, committing, and pushing.

rules.quote: **Force-push your history** (you reject the remote shape): confirm with user first — this is destructive to shared state.
rules.rule: If you reject the remote shape and choose to force-push your history, confirm with the user first because it is destructive to shared state.

rules.quote: **Never** silently rebase against a divergent remote and resolve conflicts blind; the resulting commit will contain content the user didn't intend.
rules.rule: Never silently rebase against a divergent remote.

rules.quote: **Never** silently rebase against a divergent remote and resolve conflicts blind; the resulting commit will contain content the user didn't intend.
rules.rule: Never resolve conflicts blind when rebasing against a divergent remote.

rules.quote: **Anti-pattern:** running `git pull --rebase` or `git rebase origin/BRANCH` as a reflex when push is rejected, without checking whether the remote is a force-push/squash.
rules.rule: Do not reflexively run `git pull --rebase` or `git rebase origin/BRANCH` when push is rejected without first checking whether the remote is a force-push or squash.

rules.quote: The catch-all `app.get("*")` and static middleware `app.use(express.static)` MUST be registered AFTER all API routes.
rules.rule: Register the catch-all `app.get("*")` and `express.static` middleware after all API routes.

rules.quote: When adding new API routes, always register them before any `app.use("*")` or `app.use(express.static)` middleware.
rules.rule: When adding new API routes, always register them before any `app.use("*")` or `app.use(express.static)` middleware.

rules.quote: Keep a separate short-path clone of the repo for deployments.
rules.rule: Keep a separate short-path clone of the repository for deployments.

rules.quote: Keep `C:\railway-deploy` as a dedicated `git clone` of the project's origin.
rules.rule: Keep `C:\railway-deploy` as a dedicated `git clone` of the project's origin for deployments.

rules.quote: On deploy: `cd C:\railway-deploy && git pull origin BRANCH && railway up --detach`.
rules.rule: On deploy, run `cd C:\railway-deploy && git pull origin BRANCH && railway up --detach`.

rules.quote: When linked service is lost (fresh clone, new machine), use `railway service link "SERVICE_NAME"` once
rules.rule: When the linked Railway service is lost (e.g., fresh clone or new machine), run `railway service link "SERVICE_NAME"` once.

rules.quote: Force-redeploy from the Railway dashboard.
rules.rule: If API endpoints return HTML after a deploy, force-redeploy from the Railway dashboard.

rules.quote: After any server.js change affecting routing, always verify `/api/version` returns JSON (not HTML) before declaring the deploy done.
rules.rule: After any server.js change affecting routing, always verify `/api/version` returns JSON (not HTML) before declaring the deploy done.

rules.quote: Dockerfile MUST contain `RUN npm ci && npm run build` in the same stage that runs `node server.js`.
rules.rule: Dockerfile MUST contain `RUN npm ci && npm run build` in the same stage that runs `node server.js`.

rules.quote: For an SPA: `API routes → express.static → app.get("*") catch-all → 404 handler → error handler`.
rules.rule: For an SPA, register Express middleware in this order: API routes, then `express.static`, then the `app.get("*")` catch-all, then the 404 handler, then the error handler.

rules.quote: The 404 handler must come AFTER static, not before.
rules.rule: Register the Express 404 handler after `express.static`, not before it.

rules.quote: If `/` returns 404 but `/api/*` works, check the 404 body.
rules.rule: When `/` returns 404 but `/api/*` works, check the 404 response body.

rules.quote: Boot the server locally and curl every endpoint that matters — especially the one that's broken — BEFORE pushing a server-side fix.
rules.rule: Before pushing a server-side fix, boot the server locally and curl every endpoint that matters, especially the broken one.

rules.quote: `PORT=3457 node server.js &` → `curl localhost:3457/` + `curl localhost:3457/api/version` → confirm expected body + status → stop → THEN commit/push.
rules.rule: Before committing/pushing, start the server with `PORT=3457 node server.js &`, curl `localhost:3457/` and `localhost:3457/api/version`, confirm the expected body and status, then stop the server.

rules.quote: Don't skip for "trivial" reorderings
rules.rule: Do not skip local validation even for "trivial" reorderings.

rules.quote: Run `npm run lint` before every commit.
rules.rule: Run `npm run lint` before every commit.

rules.quote: Don't let lint errors accumulate.
rules.rule: Do not let lint errors accumulate.

rules.quote: Before implementing, state ONE alternative approach and why you chose this one.
rules.rule: Before implementing a task, state one alternative approach and explain why you chose the current one.

rules.quote: Exit criteria must include runtime command, not file count.
rules.rule: Write exit criteria around a runtime command rather than a count of files created.

rules.quote: Every exit criteria block MUST include one edge case.
rules.rule: Every exit criteria block must include at least one edge case to verify.

rules.quote: Coordinator ALWAYS uses compressed format
rules.rule: Always use the compressed instruction format when handing work off.

rules.quote: No context repetition
rules.rule: When sending compressed-format instructions, do not repeat context.

rules.quote: Never send: "improve the pipeline" — too vague for M3
rules.rule: Never send vague directives such as "improve the pipeline".

rules.quote: Route to DeepSeek V4 Pro (not M3) when task involves:
rules.rule: Route tasks involving architecture decisions with multiple valid approaches to DeepSeek V4 Pro instead of M3.

rules.quote: Route to DeepSeek V4 Pro (not M3) when task involves:
rules.rule: Route tasks involving refactoring with ambiguous scope to DeepSeek V4 Pro instead of M3.

rules.quote: Route to DeepSeek V4 Pro (not M3) when task involves:
rules.rule: Route tasks involving debugging without a clear error message to DeepSeek V4 Pro instead of M3.

rules.quote: Only save lessons that would genuinely surprise a developer joining a new project.
rules.rule: In memory files, only save lessons that would genuinely surprise a developer joining a new project.

rules.quote: Skip: obvious knowledge, language fundamentals, platform basics, and project diaries.
rules.rule: When writing memory files, skip obvious knowledge, language fundamentals, platform basics, and project diaries.

rules.quote: Fit the file on one screen.
rules.rule: Keep each memory file short enough to fit on one screen.

rules.quote: Always Sync Local with Remote Before Auditing Code
rules.rule: Always sync local code with the remote before auditing code.

rules.quote: Before touching any codebase, run `git fetch + git log --oneline origin/main`.
rules.rule: Before touching any codebase, run `git fetch + git log --oneline origin/main`.

rules.quote: Every session start — fetch first, audit second, change third.
rules.rule: At every session start, fetch from the remote first, audit second, and change third.

rules.quote: Never Trust `x-user-role` from Request Headers

rules.quote: Check "Sprint Progress" table below for current status
rules.rule: When opening a new session to continue work, check the "Sprint Progress" table for the current sprint status.

rules.quote: Open the relevant skill/rule file for the sprint you're working
rules.rule: When working on a sprint, open the skill or rule file relevant to that sprint.

rules.quote: Execute the "Sprint Actions" from the section below
rules.rule: When continuing work, execute the "Sprint Actions" listed in the relevant sprint section.

rules.quote: Update the "Sprint Progress" table when done
rules.rule: When a sprint is done, update the "Sprint Progress" table.

rules.quote: Commit changes before closing session
rules.rule: Before closing a session, commit the changes.

rules.quote: You do NOT need to re-research
rules.rule: If compaction fires mid-sprint, you are not required to re-research the topic.

rules.quote: re-read this plan
rules.rule: If compaction fires mid-sprint, re-read this plan.

rules.quote: Pick up from where you left off.
rules.rule: If this session ends and you resume in a new session, resume from the point where you left off.

rules.quote: Read memory/checkpoint.yaml
rules.rule: If memory/checkpoint.yaml exists, read it when resuming.

rules.quote: Start fresh from the Sprint Progress table
rules.rule: If memory/checkpoint.yaml does not exist, start from the "Sprint Progress" table.

rules.quote: If you later expand to multi-agent with background agents, revisit this.
rules.rule: If you later expand to a multi-agent setup with background agents, revisit the mail delivery guarantee.

rules.quote: For now, skip.
rules.rule: For now, skip the Sprint 5 mail delivery guarantee and take no action on it.

rules.quote: No new tools needed — adapt existing OSS.
rules.rule: Adapt existing open-source software rather than introducing new tools.

rules.quote: don't copy, reference only
rules.rule: Do not copy Claude Code's auto-memory implementation; use it only as a reference.

rules.quote: Before any `docker compose` command, verify daemon is up:
rules.rule: Before running any `docker compose` command, verify the Docker daemon is up.

rules.quote: If error → restart Docker Desktop before proceeding
rules.rule: If the Docker daemon check returns an error, restart Docker Desktop before proceeding.

rules.quote: Wait for postgres to be ready
rules.rule: After starting services, wait for Postgres to be ready.

rules.quote: don't run migrations immediately
rules.rule: Do not run migrations immediately after starting services.

rules.quote: Run migrations (only after postgres is ready)
rules.rule: Run migrations only after Postgres is ready.

rules.quote: Wait for: "database system is ready to accept connections"
rules.rule: Before running migrations, wait for the Postgres log message "database system is ready to accept connections".

rules.quote: Review the generated file in alembic/versions/ BEFORE applying
rules.rule: Review the generated Alembic migration file in alembic/versions before applying it.

rules.quote: ALWAYS backup first
rules.rule: For a breaking migration such as a column rename or type change, always back up the database first.

rules.quote: Only use `down -v` on schema changes.
rules.rule: Only use `docker compose down -v` on schema changes.

rules.quote: Never on normal restarts.
rules.rule: Never use `docker compose down -v` on normal restarts.

rules.quote: Migration changes still need `alembic upgrade head`.
rules.rule: After migration changes, still run `alembic upgrade head`.

rules.quote: Always use Docker
rules.rule: Always use Docker for the FastAPI backend.

rules.quote: never run FastAPI directly
rules.rule: Never run FastAPI directly.

rules.quote: Add `D:\Temp\playwright-browsers` to Defender exclusions
rules.rule: Add `D:\Temp\playwright-browsers` to Windows Defender exclusions.

rules.quote: `docker compose down -v` then `up -d`
rules.rule: If the Postgres volume has a stale schema after a schema change, run `docker compose down -v` then `docker compose up -d`.

rules.quote: `docker compose down` then `up -d`
rules.rule: If an old container is still running and causing a backend port conflict, run `docker compose down` then `docker compose up -d`.

rules.quote: Restart Docker Desktop, then `docker compose up -d`
rules.rule: If the Docker daemon pipe drops, restart Docker Desktop and then run `docker compose up -d`.

rules.quote: `APP_KEY` must be generated once: `docker compose exec backend php artisan key:generate`
rules.rule: Generate the Laravel `APP_KEY` once using `docker compose exec backend php artisan key:generate`.

rules.quote: Frontend `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` must match backend Railway URL on deploy
rules.rule: On deploy, ensure the frontend `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` matches the backend Railway URL.

rules.quote: verify PostgreSQL RLS policies before any production deploy
rules.rule: Before any production deploy, verify PostgreSQL RLS policies for FERPA compliance.

rules.quote: Same patterns apply.
rules.rule: Apply the same Docker Compose local development patterns to EduFlow.

rules.quote: Check daemon is alive (`docker info`)
rules.rule: Before running Docker Compose commands, check that the Docker daemon is alive using `docker info`.

rules.quote: Know which command destroys volumes (`down -v`) and which doesn't (`down`)
rules.rule: Know which Docker Compose command destroys volumes (`down -v`) and which does not (`down`).

rules.quote: Never run backend/frontend directly on Windows
rules.rule: Never run the backend or frontend directly on Windows.

rules.quote: For schema changes: backup first
rules.rule: For schema changes, back up the database first.

rules.quote: then migrate
rules.rule: For schema changes, run migrations after backing up.

rules.quote: then verify
rules.rule: For schema changes, verify after migrating.

rules.quote: keep container node_modules separate
rules.rule: Keep the container's `node_modules` separate when mounting the Next.js frontend.

rules.quote: All services should show "running"
rules.rule: After starting services, verify that all services show "running".

rules.quote: Confirm it's a proxy problem, not a server problem
rules.rule: When diagnosing a WebSocket connection on Railway that connects but then drops, confirm whether the issue is a proxy problem rather than a server problem.

rules.quote: From a machine outside Railway
rules.rule: When testing a Railway WebSocket connection, run the test from a machine outside Railway.

rules.quote: Check Railway logs for the upgrade request
rules.rule: Check Railway logs for the WebSocket upgrade request.

rules.quote: Verify PORT env var is correct
rules.rule: Verify that the PORT environment variable is correct.

rules.quote: Switch to Server-Sent Events (SSE) for read-only streams
rules.rule: As a workaround for Railway WebSocket proxy failures, use Server-Sent Events (SSE) for read-only streams.

rules.quote: Poll every 2-3s via regular HTTP
rules.rule: As a simple fallback for Railway WebSocket proxy failures, poll every 2-3 seconds via regular HTTP.

rules.quote: Add a separate Railway service as a TCP proxy
rules.rule: When escalating to a TCP proxy on Railway, add a separate Railway service as a TCP proxy.

rules.quote: See Railway docs: Private Networking + TCP Proxy
rules.rule: Consult the Railway docs on Private Networking and TCP Proxy when evaluating a TCP proxy workaround.

rules.quote: Never promise WebSocket will work on Railway without testing first
rules.rule: When working on any Railway-deployed real-time feature, never promise that WebSocket will work on Railway without testing it first.

rules.quote: Default to SSE for server-push scenarios
rules.rule: When working on any Railway-deployed real-time feature, default to SSE for server-push scenarios.

rules.quote: Default to polling for low-frequency updates
rules.rule: When working on any Railway-deployed real-time feature, default to polling for low-frequency updates.

rules.quote: Only escalate to TCP proxy if truly bidirectional and high-frequency
rules.rule: When working on any Railway-deployed real-time feature, only escalate to a TCP proxy if the communication is truly bidirectional and high-frequency.

rules.quote: SSE for coin updates
rules.rule: For Palma Coin, prefer SSE for coin updates.

rules.quote: HTTP polling for votes
rules.rule: For Palma Coin, prefer HTTP polling for votes.
